pr_title: sql: fix system.namespace and crdb_internal.zones in 19.2 mixed-version state
pr_body:
Fixes #47167.

Previously, the system.namespace table would become inaccessible by 19.2
nodes following a 20.1 node joining the cluster. This was because of a
mistake in the namespace migration, which edited the original
system.namespace descriptor (id 2) to have its Name field set to
namespace_deprecated. This caused 19.2 nodes not to recognize it. The
reason that the migration did this (see 3c0671c) is that it's illegal
to have two descriptors with the same Name field.

This commit fixes the problem by writing the new namespace descriptor
(id 30) with a Name field set to a new value,
namespace2. This avoids the duplicate descriptor name
problem, but introduces a slight new hiccup, which is that the new
descriptor has a different Name than its actual table name, which
remains "namespace". This patch avoids this problem with a special
case. All of this special case logic can be removed in 20.2. We will
need to write a new migration for 20.2 anyway, that migrates old
namespace entries into the new format. That migration should also change
the Name of the namespace descriptor back to "namespace". The 20.1 code
will be resilient to this change, because the Name of the new namespace
descriptor is never read by 20.1.

One more detail is that this commit changes the migration key for the
migration that used to overwrite the old namespace descriptor's name
field, so that clusters that upgraded to an earlier 20.1 beta will stop
experiencing problems after changing to this version.

Release note (bug fix): fix reads from system.namespace and
crdb_internal.zones in 19.2 nodes in mixed cluster settings.

issue_context.title: sql: system.namespace is unreadable from 19.2 nodes in mixed version state
issue_context.body:
19.2 nodes in a mixed-version state with 20.1 can't read `system.descriptor` from SQL. This has cascading problems, because `crdb_internal.zones` explicitly reads `system.descriptor`, and a few things explicitly read `crdb_internal.zones`, including debug zips, admin ui, and so on.

The cause of this is that #44006 edits the `system.namespace` descriptor (which is descriptor ID 2, which is called `namespace_deprecated` in 20.1) to changes its name to `namespace_deprecated` for the purpose of making Backup not fail due to seeing descriptors with duplicate names. But the 19.2 (and prior) code expects the original `namespace` table to be named `namespace`, and does not resolve it otherwise.
comments:
Looking at this, the issue that #44006 was fixing was that the original migration added a second desc with the same name (`namespace`) and the same parent (system) which violated a contract that BACKUP and RESTORE was assuming -- that names were unique within a DB. This is because BACKUP loads all descs and then builds a map from name to ID from the descriptors (reusing the same resolution as RESTORE, where we need to run that logic on the descriptors from the backup). If we introduce a duplicate name (adding a desc at ID 30 with the name `namespace` while the desc at ID 2 also has that name), all backups in that cluster, at least on 19.2 nodes, will start to fail (backup loads all descs to build that map, so even unrelated backups of any table will see the dupe and error out).

The way #44006 fixed it was to change the name _in_ the old namespace desc (at ID2) when it created the new desc at 30 with that name. However as we see here, 19.2 nodes will still resolve that ID 2 descriptor as the descriptor for `system.namespace`, and then be confused.

We know we can't have duplicates, and we know we can't change the name in ID 2, so I think what we need to do is change the name in ID30, creating it with a new name like `namespace_with_parent` or something.

_Then_, when the cluster version ticks up (in the new thing sql-schema folks added to do the jobs migration post upgrade finalize), then we can do the swap -- rename the ID 2 table to _deprecated (or just drop it?) and rename `namespace_with_parent` to `namespace`?

I guess last question there though would be what does 20.1 resolve for `system.namespace` until then ? If it is 30, it is also going to dislike the name mis-match?

> I guess last question there though would be what does 20.1 resolve for system.namespace until then ? If it is 30, it is also going to dislike the name mis-match?

As long as the descriptor on disk's name != the name we lookup the descriptor with we're going to error out (unless we add a special case)
Yeah, I think we might need a special case for that part, but at least that is a 20.1 special case and I think can be pretty narrowly scoped.
